slides.title: Why food costs more in north & east Ethiopia
slides.body: A late harvest, failed rains and conflict, explained

slides.title: higher sorghum prices in Sekota
slides.body: White sorghum in Sekota (Wag Himra, Amhara) cost 50% more in August 2026 than a year earlier.

slides.title: above the five-year average
slides.body: Same market, same month. FEWS NET links it to low supply, a delayed harvest and high fuel costs.

slides.title: The harvest is at least a month late
slides.body: In late September many crops in Tigray were still flowering. Families must keep buying food at markets for longer.

slides.title: estimated crop losses in Hararghe
slides.body: In East and West Hararghe. Rainfall in the worst-hit areas was 50% or less of average.

slides.title: Conflict adds pressure
slides.body: Fighting along roads and in towns is disrupting fuel, markets and transport, FEWS NET says. Food aid in Tigray had targeted 1.1 million+ people since July.

slides.title: Keep food, fuel and aid routes open
slides.body: Follow for sourced updates from across Ethiopia.
